smell_validity.evidence: The injection makes the registry owner absorb transport construction, key negotiation, verification, login, presence sweeping and fan-out — three pools grow to nine fields with ECDH session, keepalive map and start-once guard, seven methods to fourteen, reached from four layers. Deleted hunks show the prior healthy split; the on-call and review pain needs no smell label. Clearly beyond mere coordination.

maintenance_impact.evidence: A lasting trap, not a local edit: verify, auth, construction, presence and fan-out collide in one type over shared locks, so changing one concern forces reading the rest; empty per-request stubs misdirect readers toward where logic no longer lives. Splitting restores per-concern ownership. No demonstrated repeated stale-behavior or inconsistent-rule driver, so not 5.

development_plausibility.evidence: Absorbed bodies are verbatim existing code riding the pre-existing ConnectionLogic singleton; added comments copy repository style, go-zero stubs and sync.Once idioms are native, and the story anchors to this repo's real commits 3369ce1 and b1e0a0b. A hardening-sprint consolidation for 'fewer places to know a connection' is a believable compromise, with no visible task-shaped scaffolding.

prompt_accuracy.evidence: It matches the injected owner method-for-method and enumerates every absorbed responsibility, making partial cleanup visible. The preservation boundary pins concrete tree specifics — per-transport registration timing, pool transitions, callback moments, lazy sweep, close codes, success lists — precisely the silent failures no gateway test catches; explicit decomposition freedom and the internal-API waiver fence off wrong direction and redesign.

semantic_diversity.evidence: Six concern clusters need distinct decisions: per-transport builders with connect-time keypairs; success-only verify transition after header rewrite; auth firing login on all paths plus offline-on-cancel; presence map with lazily once-started config-driven sweeper; success-list fan-out writes; close-only kicks. Stub reinstatement, handler orchestration and singleton wiring each add their own constraints.

localization_burden.evidence: The hub and prompt largely name the clusters, but classification demands the ConnectionLogic singleton alias, data-channel open-callback registration and config-selected sweep timing. Plausible decoys need excluding: loopCheck's separate registry sweeper, the no-op zrpc shells, untouched bookkeeping methods. Two indirect mechanisms never have to be combined for one location decision.

repair_coordination.evidence: Interacting rules: keypair creation must track verify's use of Connection.ServerPublicKey; the keepalive map must move with its sweeper while the request-triggered once-start survives; auth extraction must preserve all-paths login and pool-transition ordering through the registry owner. Repairing one side alone still compiles, so cross-site agreement is mandatory.

mechanical_resistance.evidence: A uniform return-to-request-shell rule cleanly covers roughly a quarter of sites: the stateless write/kick fan-out pair; verify/auth returns add handler-side transition decisions. Construction shares the ECDH field with verify, and the keepalive map and once-guard span intake and sweeper, so moves need per-cluster state decisions rather than one rule.

behavioral_risk.evidence: The prompt's own execution record: only go test ./common/utils/ runs; no gateway assertions exist and wrong edits compile. Two hidden paths: losing the folded all-paths login transitions when auth is regrouped (fails only cancelled or failed logins), and presence splits that move the map without the once-guard, mis-timing offline sweeps until KeepAliveSecond elapses.

recommendation_reason: Deterministic validation passed and every Quality dimension meets the retention threshold.
